Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the period-end financial reporting process (PEFRP) control set — journal-entry review, account reconciliation, consolidation and management review of the statements; SOX Program Manager owns the RACM and the test calendar

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — SOX §404 and SEC Interpretive Release 33-8810 (period-end financial reporting process and significant estimates) re-read at the September scoping refresh, alongside Form 8-K Item 4.02 (non-reliance) and PCAOB AS 2201 for auditor scoping alignment

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly and annual close: journal-entry preparation and approval, balance-sheet account reconciliation and certification, actuarial reserve roll-forward posting, inter-company elimination and consolidation, STAT-to-GAAP bridge, and management review of the statements, footnotes and disclosure checklist

In-scope systems.value: GL as book of record for all entries and the trial balance; BlackLine for reconciliation certification and close tasks; the consolidation tool for eliminations and the reporting pack

Compliance procedure documented.value: Period-End Close Control Narrative plus RACM controls PEFRP-01 to PEFRP-12 (JE approval thresholds, reconciliation aging and certification, elimination review, estimate review, disclosure-checklist tie-out), each with a flowchart, IPE listing and test attributes

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and countersigned by the Chief Financial Officer at the annual SOX scoping refresh, and re-approved out of cycle on any close-calendar change, chart-of-accounts change or GL configuration release

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Close calendar days 1-8: JE cut-off day 3, reconciliations certified day 6, consolidation locked day 7, management review memo day 8 — backed off the 10-Q (40 days after quarter end) and 10-K (60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer) due dates

Deadline reminders configured.value: BlackLine close-task reminders to each preparer and approver at day -2, day 0 and day +1, plus AuditBoard control-owner notices 10 business days before each quarter's PEFRP test window opens

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed JE approval logs with support, certified reconciliations and aging schedules, elimination workbooks, estimate review memos and the management review memo retained 7 years under Exchange Act Rule 17a-4 and PCAOB AS 1215 audit-documentation expectations

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each control failure logged with root cause, compensating control and remediation date, and rated inconsequential / significant deficiency / material weakness; anything that could make prior statements unreliable is routed to the 8-K Item 4.02 assessment

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs the deficiency severity conclusion and the remediation closure evidence before the quarter's §302 certification is executed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All manual, top-side and consolidation journal entries posted to the GL in the quarter; every balance-sheet account in the reconciliation inventory; and each legal entity's consolidation and elimination run for the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any manual JE at or above the $250,000 posting threshold without an approver independent of the preparer is a fail; any reconciliation certified more than 30 days after period end, or certified by its own preparer, is a fail; a single failure on a top-side or estimate-driven entry triggers an immediate significant-deficiency assessment

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs every close; PEFRP controls are tested interim in Q2 and Q3 and roll-forward tested over the Q4/annual close so the conclusion supports the Item 9A assessment in the 10-K

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Tester must not have prepared, reviewed or approved any journal entry, reconciliation or consolidation run in the period under test

Evidence location for test results.value: AuditBoard workpaper PEFRP-Qx holding the JE population extract with row counts, the seeded sample selection, re-performance notes, IPE completeness evidence and the exception schedule

Regulator-ready documentation.value: RACM, walkthrough narratives, test workpapers, deficiency log and the management ICFR assessment supporting Item 9A and Reg S-K Item 308(a)(3), producible for the external auditor or a PCAOB inspection within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Controller answers close-control questions with the SOX Program Manager; the Audit Committee and General Counsel clear any non-reliance (8-K Item 4.02) determination or SEC comment-letter response before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Refresh ICFR scope and pin the period-end close controls into it
actions: Pull the prior-year trial balance from the Controller and compute planning materiality and the performance-materiality threshold used to scope accounts.

In AuditBoard open Scoping ▸ Entities & Accounts and mark every account over threshold plus every account with a significant estimate (loss reserves, DAC, investment impairment, deferred tax) as in-scope regardless of size.
Flag the period-end financial reporting process as a required scope area under SEC Release 33-8810 and attach the release excerpt to the scoping memo.
Map PEFRP-01 to PEFRP-12 to the in-scope accounts and assertions so no scoped account is left without a close control.
Circulate the scoping memo to the external audit engagement partner and record their scope-alignment response.
checklist.done: the signed scoping memo lists every in-scope account, names PEFRP as a scoped process, and has the auditor's alignment response attached.

checklist.step: Publish the close calendar and name an owner for every close control
actions: In BlackLine open Task Management ▸ Templates and set the day-1 to day-8 close task list for the quarter with entity, preparer, reviewer and due day on each task.
Set the hard gates: JE cut-off close day 3, reconciliation certification close day 6, consolidation lock close day 7, management review close day 8.
Back the calendar off the filing dates — 40 days after quarter end for the 10-Q and 60 days after fiscal year end for the 10-K — and show the slack days on the calendar.
Send the calendar to entity controllers, the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Reserving Actuary and get written acceptance of their task dates.
Configure task reminders at day -2, day 0 and day +1 for each assignee.
checklist.done: the quarter's close calendar is published in BlackLine with every task owned, dated and accepted, and reminders armed.

checklist.step: Enforce the journal-entry cut-off and the approval threshold matrix
actions: In the GL open the period-close screen and confirm the sub-ledger cut-off dates for AP, AR, premium, claims and investments match the close calendar.
Verify the JE workflow configuration still enforces preparer-cannot-approve segregation and routes entries at or above $250,000 to a second approver at Controller level.
Request the current GL approval-role assignment listing from the ERP security administrator and confirm no leavers or transfers retain posting rights.
Close each sub-ledger on its calendar day and record the close timestamp; post-cut-off entries require a written Controller exception with reason.
File the configuration screenshots and the role listing as IPE support for control PEFRP-03.
checklist.done: sub-ledgers are closed on their calendar days, the approval matrix is evidenced by dated configuration and role listings, and every post-cut-off entry has a written exception.

checklist.step: Prepare, support and route manual and top-side journal entries
actions: Enter each manual JE in the GL with a business rationale in the header text, the source of the amount, and the accounting basis (GAAP reference or policy paragraph).
Attach the computation workbook and the third-party or sub-ledger support to the JE record — no entry is submitted with an empty attachment slot.
Route top-side and consolidation-level entries to the Controller rather than the entity reviewer, and tag them TOPSIDE in the JE type field.
Hand the daily unposted-JE listing to the reviewer each close day so nothing sits unapproved past the cut-off.
Export the posted-JE listing for the period into the close folder as the population source for later testing.
checklist.done: every manual and top-side entry is posted with rationale, support and a documented independent approver, and the posted-JE listing is exported.

checklist.step: Certify balance-sheet account reconciliations and clear aged items
actions: In BlackLine open Account Reconciliations and confirm every account in the reconciliation inventory has an assigned preparer and an independent approver.
Reconcile each account to its source of record — sub-ledger, bank statement, custodian statement, actuarial reserve report or reinsurance ceded ledger — and attach that source to the reconciliation.
Age reconciling items and escalate any item over 90 days or over the account's risk threshold to the Controller with a written clearance plan.
Certify reconciliations by close day 6; auto-certification rules must be evidenced by their configuration and limited to zero-balance and fully-matched accounts.
Export the certification status report showing preparer, approver and certification date for the period.
checklist.done: all inventory accounts are reconciled to a named source, certified by day 6 by someone other than the preparer, and aged items carry a dated clearance plan.

checklist.step: Post and control the actuarial reserve roll-forward into the ledger
actions: Deliver the signed reserve roll-forward (beginning reserves, incurred current year, incurred prior years, paid, ending reserves) by line of business to the Controller on the close-calendar date.
Reconcile the ending carried reserve in the actuarial report to the GL reserve accounts line by line and explain every difference over the reporting threshold in writing.
Attach the reserve committee minutes and the selected-estimate rationale as the significant-estimate evidence required by Release 33-8810.
Confirm the booked reserve sits within the actuarial range and record the Appointed Actuary's concurrence where it does not sit at the central estimate.
Hand the reconciliation and the concurrence memo to the Controller for the management review file.
checklist.done: the GL reserve balance ties to the signed actuarial roll-forward, differences are explained, and the estimate rationale and concurrence are on file.

checklist.step: Run consolidation and clear inter-company eliminations
actions: Load each legal entity's trial balance into the consolidation tool and run the validation report for unmapped accounts and out-of-balance entities before consolidating.
Run the inter-company matching report, chase unmatched balances with the counterparty entity controller, and clear or accrue every difference above the elimination threshold.
Post elimination and currency-translation entries with support, and route them to the Controller as top-side entries.
Reconcile consolidated equity and net income to the sum of entity results plus documented eliminations and confirm the roll-forward proves out to the prior period.
Lock the consolidation on close day 7 and export the locked reporting pack to the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: the consolidation is locked with zero unmapped accounts, all inter-company differences cleared or explained, and equity and net income proving to the prior period.

checklist.step: Document the significant-estimate review and the management review controls
actions: For each significant estimate — loss and LAE reserves, DAC recoverability, investment credit impairment, goodwill, deferred tax valuation allowance — record the method, key assumptions, the range considered and why the booked point was selected.
State the review precision on the management review control: the threshold at which a variance is investigated, expressed in dollars and in percent, not as 'reviewed for reasonableness'.
Evidence the review with the reviewer's annotated variance analysis showing questions raised, answers received and the resolution.
Collect the sub-certifications from entity controllers, the Reserving Actuary, Tax and Investments confirming completeness of their inputs.
File the estimate memos and sub-certifications into the management review file for the period.
checklist.done: each significant estimate has a documented method, assumption set and selection rationale, and the management review evidences precision and follow-up, not just a signature.

checklist.step: Tie the statements and footnotes to the disclosure checklist
actions: Build the tie-out binder linking every face-of-statement and footnote number to the locked consolidation pack or a supporting schedule reference.

Work the GAAP disclosure checklist for insurance entities (ASC 944 reserve and DAC disclosures, ASC 320/326 investment disclosures, ASC 740 tax rate reconciliation) and mark each line complete, not applicable with reason, or open.
Re-foot and cross-cast the statements and confirm the XBRL tagging in the filing tool matches the tied-out numbers element by element.
Circulate the tied-out draft to the Disclosure Committee with the changes-from-prior-period summary highlighted.
Store the signed binder in the financial reporting repository under the period.
checklist.done: every reported number traces to the locked pack or a referenced schedule, the disclosure checklist is fully dispositioned, and the binder is signed and filed.

checklist.step: Prepare the NAIC statutory statements and reconcile STAT to GAAP
actions: Load the entity trial balances into the statutory reporting tool against the correct NAIC annual or quarterly blank for the line (Property & Casualty, Life/Fraternal, Health) and run the NAIC cross-check edits.
Clear every failed cross-check and jurat, exhibit and schedule edit — record an explanation for any edit overridden.

Build the STAT-to-GAAP bridge showing non-admitted assets, deferred acquisition cost differences, reserve basis differences and deferred tax differences, and reconcile statutory surplus to GAAP equity.
Give the bridge and the blank draft to the Controller for review against the locked GAAP consolidation pack.

File the reviewed blanks with the state of domicile and the NAIC by the statutory deadlines — March 1 for the annual statement and the 15th day of the second month after each of the first three quarters.
checklist.done: the blanks pass NAIC cross-checks with no unexplained overrides, statutory surplus reconciles to GAAP equity, and filing confirmations are captured.

checklist.step: Test the period-end close controls inside the quarter
actions: Request the posted-JE listing and the reconciliation certification report from the Controller and validate their completeness against GL record counts before sampling (IPE testing).
Select samples per the AuditBoard test plan attributes and re-perform each attribute — approver independence, threshold routing, support attached, certification date, aged-item clearance.
Photograph or export the GL and BlackLine screens showing the approver identity and timestamp into the workpaper rather than relying on a summary report.
Raise a test exception the same day it is identified and notify the control owner with the specific record id.
Update control conclusions in AuditBoard to effective / effective with exceptions / not effective.
checklist.done: every PEFRP control has a completed test with IPE support, evidenced attributes and a recorded conclusion for the quarter.

checklist.step: Evaluate deficiencies and rate their severity
actions: For each exception assess the potential magnitude against performance materiality and the likelihood of a misstatement not being prevented or detected on a timely basis.
Rate the deficiency inconsequential, significant deficiency or material weakness, and write the reasoning in those terms rather than asserting the rating.
Aggregate related deficiencies across controls — several individually inconsequential close failures affecting the same account can aggregate to a significant deficiency.
Agree the rating with the external auditor and log any difference of view with both positions stated.
Assign an owner and a remediation date to each rated deficiency and set a retest date inside the same fiscal year.
checklist.done: each deficiency carries a written severity rationale, an aggregation assessment, an owner, a remediation date and a retest date.

checklist.step: Assess whether a non-reliance determination is triggered
actions: Where an error is identified in previously issued statements, quantify it under both the rollover and iron-curtain methods and assess materiality quantitatively and qualitatively.
Convene the Audit Committee with the Controller, General Counsel and the external auditor to decide reliance versus non-reliance.
If the statements should no longer be relied upon, file a Form 8-K Item 4.02(a) within four business days of the determination and state the affected periods.
Where the error is immaterial, document the SAB 99 analysis and the revise-in-future-filings decision instead.
Record the decision, the participants and the date in the Audit Committee minutes.
checklist.done: any identified error has a documented materiality analysis, an Audit Committee decision, and either an 8-K Item 4.02 filed within four business days or a documented immateriality conclusion.

checklist.step: Support the external auditor's walkthrough and roll-forward procedures
actions: Deliver the PEFRP narratives, flowcharts and RACM to the audit team before the interim walkthrough date and walk each control end to end with the named control owner present.
Track auditor requests on the prepared-by-client list with owner and due date and close them inside the agreed turnaround.
Provide the roll-forward evidence for the period between interim testing and year end — no gap month may be left untested.
Reconcile the auditor's deficiency list to the internal deficiency log and resolve every item present on one list only.
Obtain the auditor's ICFR opinion draft and confirm it is consistent with the management assessment before the 10-K is finalised.
checklist.done: the auditor's walkthroughs and roll-forward are complete, the PBC list is closed, and the auditor and management deficiency lists and ICFR conclusions agree.

checklist.step: Retain the close and ICFR evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the period close folder — JE listings and approvals, certified reconciliations, elimination workbooks, estimate memos, tie-out binder, statutory blanks and filing confirmations — into the evidence repository indexed by entity and period.
Apply the 7-year retention label consistent with Exchange Act Rule 17a-4 and confirm the legal-hold flag is honoured where litigation holds exist.
Verify the index makes the record searchable by entity, period, control id and account number.
Run the retention completeness report and chase any close artifact listed on the calendar but missing from the repository.
checklist.done: the complete period close and ICFR evidence set is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, and retrievable by entity, period and control id.

testing.step: Build the population of journal entries and reconciliations for the period
actions: Extract directly from the GL — not from a prepared file — every journal entry posted with a posting date in the quarter, with preparer, approver, amount, account, entity, source and timestamp.
Extract the reconciliation inventory and certification report from BlackLine with preparer, approver, certification date and aged-item balances.
Ask the ERP administrator for the record count and control totals for the same date range and reconcile the extract to them.
Add consolidation-tool entries so top-side and elimination postings made outside the GL cannot escape the population.
testing.done: the extracted population reconciles to GL control totals and includes consolidation-level entries, and the extractor has signed the completeness statement.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the reported financial statements
actions: Foot the extracted entries by account and agree the movement to the trial balance and then to the face of the filed statements.
Agree the reconciliation inventory to the account listing behind the balance sheet and identify any balance-sheet account with no reconciliation assigned.
Trace the consolidated net income and equity in the population back to the locked consolidation pack used for filing.
Treat every unreconciled account and every unexplained difference as an automatic exception rather than a scope note.
testing.done: the population ties to the filed statements and every balance-sheet account is shown either covered by a reconciliation or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of top-side entries, consolidation entries and entries posted after the close cut-off.
Take all manual entries at or above the $250,000 approval threshold, plus 40 entries drawn at random with a recorded seed from the remaining manual population.
Take 25 reconciliations weighted to accounts with significant estimates and to accounts with aged items over 90 days.
Record the population size, the strata, the seed and the draw date in the workpaper so the selection can be reproduced.
testing.done: the sample covers 100% of top-side, post-cut-off and above-threshold entries and is reproducible from the recorded seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the journal-entry approval judgement in the general ledger
actions: Open each sampled entry in the GL document display and read the header rationale, the attached support and the workflow approval history.
Confirm the approver is not the preparer, holds an approval limit covering the amount, and approved after the support was attached rather than before.
Reach your own conclusion on whether the entry is supported by the attachment before reading the control owner's sign-off.
Capture the workflow history screen showing user ids and timestamps into the workpaper.
Log any entry with a generic rationale such as 'to true up' and no computation as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled entry has an independent re-performance note, a captured approval-history screen, and a stated supported/unsupported conclusion.

testing.step: Re-perform reconciliation certification and test the aged items
actions: Open each sampled reconciliation in BlackLine and agree the GL balance shown to the GL and the source balance to the underlying statement or actuarial report.
Recompute the reconciling items and confirm the residual difference is zero or within the documented threshold.
Check the certification date against the close-day-6 requirement and the approver identity against the preparer.
Test the clearance of items aged over 90 days by tracing them to the subsequent-period entry that cleared them.
testing.done: each sampled reconciliation is independently agreed to source, its certification date and approver independence verified, and aged items traced to clearance or logged.

testing.step: Test the significant-estimate and management review controls for precision
actions: Read the estimate memo for reserves, DAC and investment impairment and confirm the assumption set, the range considered and the selection rationale are all present and dated before the filing.
Test the stated review precision by re-computing the variance the reviewer said they investigate and confirming items over that threshold actually generated documented questions and answers.
Trace the reserve roll-forward in the memo to the GL reserve accounts and to the corresponding NAIC blank schedule.
Treat a review evidenced only by a signature, with no thresholds and no follow-up trail, as an ineffective control, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: each significant estimate shows a dated rationale and the management review evidences a stated precision threshold with follow-up questions and resolutions.

testing.step: Verify the consolidation and the STAT-to-GAAP bridge independently
actions: Re-run the inter-company matching report for the period and confirm no unmatched balance above the elimination threshold remained open at consolidation lock.
Recompute total eliminations and agree them to the elimination entries posted as top-side JEs.
Recompute the STAT-to-GAAP bridge from statutory surplus in the filed NAIC blank to GAAP equity in the filed statements, line by line.
Confirm the consolidation lock timestamp precedes the management review date and the filing date.
testing.done: eliminations, the consolidation lock timing and the statutory-to-GAAP bridge all recompute without unexplained difference.

testing.step: Recompute the close-calendar and filing deadline arithmetic
actions: Compare each close task's actual completion timestamp to its calendar due day and quantify the slippage in days.
Recompute the filing due dates — 40 days after quarter end for the 10-Q and 60 days after fiscal year end for the 10-K — and compare to the actual EDGAR acceptance timestamps.
Recompute the statutory deadlines (annual statement March 1; quarterly statements May 15, August 15 and November 15) against the NAIC and state filing confirmations.
Flag any control whose evidence is dated after the filing date, since it cannot have supported the certification that was signed.
testing.done: every close task, SEC filing and statutory filing date is recomputed and any control evidence post-dating the filing is flagged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the entry or account id, the failed attribute, the account and the dollar exposure.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — approval workflow bypass, threshold misconfiguration, missing IPE, preparer/approver conflict, calendar slippage, estimate rationale not documented — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and a retest date inside the same fiscal year so the annual conclusion is not left open.
Escalate any aggregated significant deficiency to the Audit Committee and to the external auditor within five business days of rating.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue record, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate per control and compare it to the stated thresholds, calling out any single fail on a top-side or estimate-driven entry.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references that carry it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared, reviewed or approved nothing in the tested period, sign the workpaper.
Present the conclusion and open deficiencies to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and confirm consistency with the Item 9A management assessment before the 10-K is filed.
File the signed workpaper in the evidence repository under the period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with exception rates, a stated conclusion, an independent reviewer signature and an Audit Committee reporting date recorded.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual Item 406 code-of-ethics disclosure package and the filing calendar that lands it in the 10-K and the NAIC/state annual statement cycle; Ethics Officer owns the code text itself

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Reg S-K Item 406 (17 CFR 229.406) and SOX §406 re-read at each 10-K drafting kick-off, together with Form 8-K Item 5.05 (amendments and waivers), NYSE Listed Company Manual §303A.10 and SEC Rule 10D-1 for the adjacent clawback-policy disclosure

In-scope processes.value: Annual disclosure drafting for Form 10-K Part III Item 10 and the proxy: confirming the code covers the CEO, CFO, principal accounting officer/controller and persons performing similar functions, posting the code, and the four-business-day amendment/waiver reporting path — plus the NAIC annual and quarterly statement filing cycle it shares a calendar with

In-scope systems.value: Code of ethics master version, annual attestation results and waiver register held in the evidence repository; the filed disclosure and Exhibit 14 are held with the 10-K package in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Code of Ethics Disclosure Procedure — annual scope confirmation of covered officers, code review and re-approval, Item 406 disclosure language, website posting and undertaking, waiver-and-amendment escalation with the four-business-day clock

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and the Audit Committee at the annual governance review; the code itself is re-approved by the Board of Directors and the approval date is quoted in the disclosure

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Item 406 disclosure files with the 10-K (60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer) or in the proxy incorporated by reference within 120 days of year end; any amendment or waiver is disclosed on Form 8-K Item 5.05 or on the website within four business days; the same calendar carries the NAIC annual statement (March 1) and quarterly statements (May 15, August 15, November 15)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar alerts at T-45, T-20 and T-5 business days to the 10-K filing date for the Part III Item 10 owner, and a standing same-day alert to the Corporate Secretary and General Counsel whenever a waiver request is opened, because the four-business-day clock starts on the grant

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Board approval minutes for the code, the covered-officer list, dated website-posting captures, the annual attestation extract, the waiver register and the filed Exhibit 14 retained 7 years under Exchange Act Rule 17a-4

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Code violations, waiver grants and late or missing disclosures logged with the covered officer, the provision waived, the approving body and the disclosure date, each closed against a named disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off any late Item 406 or 8-K Item 5.05 disclosure and the corrective filing before it is submitted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The filed 10-K Part III Item 10 disclosure and Exhibit 14 for the year, the full covered-officer list from HR, every waiver or amendment approved during the year, and every NAIC and state statement filed in the same annual cycle

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a missing or non-conforming Item 406 disclosure, a code not publicly available at the address the filing names, or a waiver disclosed later than four business days after grant is a fail; any single fail escalates to the Audit Committee before the next filing

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Annual disclosure is tested once per year ahead of the 10-K filing, with a quarterly sweep of the waiver register and the website posting because the four-business-day amendment obligation is event-driven

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted the disclosure, approved a waiver or maintained the covered-officer list

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Item 406 test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository holding the EDGAR filing copy, the dated website capture, the covered-officer reconciliation and the waiver-register timing recomputation

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed disclosure, Exhibit 14, board approval minutes, waiver register with disclosure dates and the website availability captures, assembled as an SEC comment-letter or state examination response within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Investor Relations Director routes SEC comment letters to the General Counsel and the Regulatory Reporting Manager; state insurance department questions on the statement filings route to the Statutory Reporting Manager, with counsel clearing any admission of a late disclosure

checklist.step: Confirm who counts as a covered officer for the year
actions: Pull the officer roster from HR and identify the principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller, and any person performing a similar function at a subsidiary that rolls into the registrant.
Compare the roster to the Section 16 filer list and the executive officer list published in the prior 10-K and resolve every name present on one list only.
Record each officer's appointment and departure dates so mid-year changes are reflected in the disclosure period.
Send the confirmed covered-officer list to the Ethics Officer and the Regulatory Reporting Manager and have them acknowledge it in writing.
checklist.done: a dated covered-officer list exists, reconciled to the HR roster and the Section 16 filer list, and acknowledged by the disclosure drafter.

checklist.step: Review the code of ethics against the Item 406 content elements
actions: Read the current code against each Item 406(b) element: honest and ethical conduct including conflicts of interest, full/fair/accurate/timely/understandable disclosure in SEC filings, compliance with applicable law, prompt internal reporting of violations, and accountability for adherence.
Mark each element to the code paragraph that satisfies it, and draft language for any element the code does not reach.
Compare the code against the NYSE Listed Company Manual §303A.10 code-of-conduct expectation so the exchange and SEC requirements are met by one document.
Circulate the redline to the General Counsel and the Chief HR Officer for comment and record their dispositions.
checklist.done: every Item 406(b) element is mapped to a specific code paragraph, gaps are drafted out, and the redline has documented legal and HR dispositions.

checklist.step: Obtain Board re-approval of the code and capture the minute
actions: Post the redlined code and the Item 406 element mapping to the board portal as a pre-read at least five business days before the meeting.
Table the code for Board or Audit Committee approval and record the resolution wording, the approval date and any conditions.
Capture the approved version number and date into the code master record so the disclosure can quote them accurately.
Distribute the approved code to the covered officers and to all employees through the standard policy channel.
checklist.done: the board minute records an approval resolution with a date and version, and the approved version is the one held as master.

checklist.step: Run the annual code attestation for covered officers and employees
actions: Assign the code training and attestation campaign in the LMS to the full employee population with a mandatory sub-campaign for the covered officers.
Set the completion deadline at least 30 days before the 10-K drafting kick-off so results are available to the disclosure.
Chase non-completers weekly through their people managers and escalate any covered officer non-completion to the General Counsel.
Export the completion report with employee id, role, completion date and any disclosed conflict, and file it in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: attestation completion is 100% for covered officers, the population report is exported and filed, and disclosed conflicts are routed to the Ethics Officer.

checklist.step: Publish the code and record where it is available
actions: Post the approved code PDF to the investor relations site under Corporate Governance and confirm the URL resolves without a login.

Decide and record the Item 406(c) availability method being relied on — website posting, Exhibit 14 filing, or an undertaking to provide the code free on request — and use the same method consistently.
Capture the posted page as a dated PDF including the URL and the code version so the filing statement can be evidenced.
Notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager of the exact URL text to quote in the disclosure.
checklist.done: the code is publicly reachable at a recorded URL, the availability method is chosen and documented, and a dated posting capture is filed.

checklist.step: Draft the Item 406 disclosure for Part III Item 10
actions: Draft the disclosure stating that a code of ethics has been adopted, naming the covered positions in Item 406(a) terms, and giving the website address where it is available.
Where the code does not apply to any covered person, state that fact and explain why — a blank is not an option under Item 406(a).
Quote the board approval date and the code version from the code master record.
Route the draft to the General Counsel and the Disclosure Committee with the prior-year language shown as a redline.
Load the approved language into the filing tool for Part III Item 10 or the proxy section incorporated by reference.
checklist.done: the Item 406 disclosure is drafted with covered positions, availability address and approval date, redlined against prior year and cleared by counsel.

checklist.step: Attach Exhibit 14 and confirm the exhibit index
actions: Where availability is being met by filing, attach the approved code as Exhibit 14 to the Form 10-K and confirm the exhibit index entry and description are correct.
Check the exhibit file is the board-approved version, not a working draft, by comparing the version stamp to the code master record.
Confirm the incorporation-by-reference language in Part III matches the proxy section actually carrying the disclosure and the proxy will be filed within 120 days of fiscal year end.
Sign off the exhibit index page for the filing package.
checklist.done: Exhibit 14 carries the board-approved version, the exhibit index is correct, and any incorporation by reference points at a proxy section that will exist in time.

checklist.step: Stand up the waiver and amendment escalation path with the four-business-day clock
actions: Document that only the Board or the Audit Committee may waive a code provision for a covered officer, and that no manager may grant one.
Instruct that the disclosure clock is four business days from the date the waiver is granted, not from the date it is documented or discovered.
Set the disclosure route: Form 8-K Item 5.05 or website posting, using the method the company disclosed it would use in its filings, and use one method consistently.
Brief the Corporate Secretary, the Ethics Officer and the Chief HR Officer on the escalation path and record their acknowledgement.
checklist.done: the waiver authority, the four-business-day clock and the single disclosure method are documented and acknowledged by the escalation owners.

checklist.step: Maintain the waiver and amendment register
actions: Open a register entry for each waiver request or code amendment with the requester, the covered officer, the code provision, the approving body and the grant date.
Compute the disclosure due date as grant date plus four business days and record it on the entry when the waiver is granted.
Record the disclosure method used, the 8-K accession number or the website posting capture, and the actual disclosure date.
Report open register entries to the Audit Committee at each meeting so nothing sits undisclosed between reporting cycles.
checklist.done: every waiver and amendment has a register entry with a grant date, a computed due date and a recorded disclosure with its accession number or posting capture.

checklist.step: Load the SEC and NAIC filing dates onto a single annual calendar
actions: Enter the SEC dates: 10-K at 60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer, 10-Q at 40 days after quarter end, proxy within 120 days of year end for Part III incorporation, and 8-K at four business days from the triggering event.
Enter the statutory dates: NAIC annual statement March 1, quarterly statements May 15, August 15 and November 15, plus the state-specific supplements the domiciliary state requires.
Name an owner and a preparer on every calendar row and set T-45, T-20 and T-5 business-day reminders.
Reconcile the calendar to the prior-year filing list so no recurring filing is dropped, and add any new filing arising from a new state licence.
checklist.done: one calendar holds every SEC and statutory due date for the year with owners, reminders and a reconciliation to the prior-year filing list.

checklist.step: File the NAIC annual and quarterly statements on the shared cycle
actions: Run the NAIC cross-check edits on the completed blank and clear every failed edit before submission.
Submit the annual statement to the NAIC and the state of domicile by March 1 and each quarterly statement by the 15th day of the second month following quarter end.
Download and file the NAIC submission confirmation and the state acknowledgement for each filing, showing the timestamp.
Mark the calendar row complete only when the confirmation is attached — a submitted-but-unconfirmed row stays open.
checklist.done: each statutory statement is filed by its deadline with an attached NAIC or state confirmation carrying a timestamp.

checklist.step: Submit the annual filing and capture the acceptance evidence
actions: Run the filing-agent validation on the 10-K package and clear all EDGAR validation errors, including Inline XBRL tagging errors on Part III where applicable.
Submit through EDGAR and capture the accession number and the acceptance timestamp.
Verify on EDGAR that the filed document actually contains the Item 406 disclosure text and the Exhibit 14 attachment as intended, by opening the filed copy rather than the submitted draft.
File the filed copy, accession number and acceptance timestamp against the calendar row.
checklist.done: the filing is accepted with a captured accession number, and the filed copy has been opened and confirmed to contain the Item 406 disclosure and exhibit.

checklist.step: Sweep the website posting each quarter
actions: Open the URL quoted in the most recent filing from an unauthenticated browser and confirm the code loads.
Compare the posted version stamp to the code master record and to the version named in the filing.
Confirm any waiver disclosed by website posting is still reachable and remains posted for the period the company committed to.
Save a dated capture including the URL into the evidence repository and raise an issue on any broken link or stale version the same day.
checklist.done: each quarter has a dated capture proving the quoted URL resolves to the version named in the filing, with issues raised on any mismatch.

checklist.step: Report code programme results to the Audit Committee
actions: Build the annual report: attestation completion rates, code violations by category and outcome, hotline volumes and trends, waivers granted and their disclosure timing, and any late filing.
Post the report to the board portal with the covered-officer list and the waiver register as appendices.
Present at the Audit Committee, capture the questions raised and any directed action with an owner and due date.
Record the reporting date in the compliance calendar as evidence the governance loop closed.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has received the annual report with attestation, violation and waiver data, and directed actions are recorded with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Retain the disclosure and filing evidence
actions: File the board approval minute, approved code version, covered-officer list, attestation extract, waiver register, website captures, filed 10-K copy with Exhibit 14, and every NAIC and state confirmation into the repository under the filing year.
Apply the 7-year retention label consistent with Exchange Act Rule 17a-4 and honour any legal hold.
Confirm the index makes records searchable by filing year, accession number, officer name and code version.
Run the completeness check against the annual filing calendar and chase any row with no confirmation attached.
checklist.done: the full year's disclosure and filing evidence set is filed, labelled for 7-year retention, and every calendar row has an attached confirmation.

testing.step: Build the population of covered officers, filings and waivers
actions: Extract the officer population from HR for the full fiscal year including joiners and leavers with effective dates.
Extract the year's filing list from EDGAR full-text search for the registrant, restricted to 10-K, 10-Q, DEF 14A and 8-K.
Extract every waiver and amendment register entry opened or closed in the year from the GRC platform.
Extract the statutory filing list from the NAIC submission log for the same year.
testing.done: the population covers officers, SEC filings, waivers and statutory filings for the full year, with extraction dates and sources recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the source of record
actions: Reconcile the HR officer extract to the executive officer list in the filed 10-K and to the Section 16 filer list and resolve every one-sided name.
Reconcile the extracted filing list to the annual filing calendar and identify any calendar row with no corresponding filing.
Reconcile the waiver register to Audit Committee and Board minutes for the year to catch a waiver granted in a meeting but never registered.
Treat any minute-approved waiver missing from the register as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the officer, filing and waiver populations reconcile to HR records, the filing calendar and board minutes, with one-sided items logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of waivers and code amendments — the population is small and the obligation is zero-tolerance.
Take 100% of the annual Item 406 disclosure and Exhibit 14 and 100% of the covered-officer list.
Take 15 statutory filings selected at random with a recorded seed, weighted to the domiciliary state and the annual statement.
Record the population sizes, the strata, the seed and the draw date so the selection is reproducible.
testing.done: the sample covers all waivers and the annual disclosure in full, plus a seeded, reproducible statutory filing sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the Item 406 disclosure judgement against the filed document
actions: Open the as-filed 10-K on EDGAR and read Part III Item 10 without first reading the internal draft.

Test the disclosure against Item 406(a): does it state adoption, name the principal executive officer, principal financial officer and principal accounting officer or controller, and either give availability or explain non-adoption?
Read the code as filed and confirm it addresses all five Item 406(b) elements, marking each to a paragraph.
Record any element addressed only by implication as an exception, including 'right answer, weak drafting'.
testing.done: the filed disclosure and code are independently mapped element by element to Item 406(a) and (b) with each gap logged.

testing.step: Test public availability from outside the company
actions: Open the URL exactly as quoted in the filing from an unauthenticated browser session on a network outside the corporate estate.
Confirm the document that loads is the board-approved version by comparing the version stamp to the board minute.
Where the company relied on the undertaking to provide the code free on request, submit a test request through the stated channel and time the response.
Capture the URL, timestamp and document version into the workpaper.
testing.done: public availability is proven from outside the corporate network, with the loaded version matched to the board-approved version.

testing.step: Recompute the four-business-day waiver disclosure clock
actions: For each waiver, read the grant date from the Board or Audit Committee minute rather than from the register field.
Recompute the due date as grant date plus four business days, excluding weekends and federal holidays.
Compare to the 8-K acceptance timestamp on EDGAR or the dated website posting capture and record the days late where applicable.
Confirm the disclosure method used matches the method the company said it would use in its filings — switching methods without disclosure is an exception.
testing.done: every waiver has a recomputed due date from the minute-recorded grant date, compared to actual disclosure, with method consistency confirmed.

testing.step: Trace the statutory filings to submission confirmations and deadlines
actions: For each sampled statutory filing, open the submission log and read the submission timestamp and the confirmation reference.
Compare the timestamp against the statutory deadline — March 1 for the annual statement, and May 15, August 15 or November 15 for the quarterly statements.
Confirm the filed blank is the version that cleared the NAIC cross-check edits, by matching the edit-clearance report reference to the submitted file.
Log any filing with an overridden edit and no written explanation as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled statutory filing traces to a timestamped confirmation inside its deadline and to a cleared cross-check report.

testing.step: Test the attestation and covered-officer completeness
actions: Match the covered-officer list to the LMS attestation completion report and confirm 100% completion by covered officers before the 10-K filing date.
Test five non-officer employees at random to confirm the campaign reached the full population, not just the executive group.
Confirm any conflict disclosed during attestation was routed to the Ethics Officer and dispositioned before the filing.
Flag any covered officer appointed mid-year who was never assigned the campaign.
testing.done: covered-officer attestation is 100% complete before the filing date, mid-year joiners are covered, and disclosed conflicts are dispositioned.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the filing, the officer or the waiver and the specific requirement missed.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — covered-officer list stale, code element not addressed, URL not maintained, waiver not escalated, calendar row unowned, statutory edit overridden — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date ahead of the next filing that would repeat the failure, and open a counsel-led assessment for any late disclosure.
Carry every open exception into the next annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date ahead of the next filing, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance threshold for a missing, non-conforming or late Item 406 disclosure.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither drafted the disclosure nor approved a waiver nor maintained the officer list, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the filing year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a stated conclusion against the zero-tolerance threshold and a recorded Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Form 10-K supplemental schedules and the exhibit index — Reg S-X Article 7 insurance schedules I to VI, Exhibit 14 code of ethics, Exhibit 97 clawback policy, Exhibits 21, 23, 31 and 32

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Reg S-X Rules 7-05 and 12-15 to 12-18 (insurance schedules), Reg S-K Item 601 (exhibit index, including Exhibit 14 under Item 406 and Exhibit 97 under Rule 10D-1), and SEC Rule 10D-1 / Exchange Act §10D re-read at each 10-K drafting kick-off

In-scope processes.value: Annual 10-K schedule and exhibit preparation: Schedule I summary of investments, Schedule II condensed parent-only financials, Schedule III supplementary insurance information, Schedule IV reinsurance, Schedule V valuation and qualifying accounts, Schedule VI P&C supplementary information, plus the exhibit index, Inline XBRL tagging and auditor consent

In-scope systems.value: Schedules built from the locked consolidation pack and the investment, reinsurance and reserve sub-ledgers; drafted, tagged and versioned in the reporting repository alongside the 10-K

Compliance procedure documented.value: Supplemental Schedules and Exhibits Procedure — per-schedule data source map, tie-out attributes, preparer/reviewer split, exhibit index build rules, XBRL tagging review and the consent and certification assembly sequence

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Controller and the Chief Financial Officer at the annual 10-K kick-off and re-approved whenever a schedule requirement changes, a legal entity is added, or the clawback policy is amended

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Schedules and exhibits must be final for the 10-K due 60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer; internal gates set schedule drafts at T-25 business days, auditor review at T-15, exhibit index and consent at T-7, and Inline XBRL review at T-5

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at T-25, T-15, T-7 and T-5 business days to each named schedule preparer, plus a standing alert to the Compensation & Benefits Manager if the clawback policy changes so Exhibit 97 is refreshed

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Schedule tie-out binders with source extracts, preparer and reviewer sign-offs, the exhibit index build sheet, the auditor consent and the as-filed schedules retained 7 years under Exchange Act Rule 17a-4

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Schedule tie-out breaks, omitted schedules, missing or stale exhibits and XBRL tagging errors logged with the schedule reference, the dollar difference and the remediation before or after filing

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off any post-filing schedule correction and the decision on whether it requires a 10-K/A amendment

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Reg S-X schedule filed with the 10-K (I, II, III, IV, V and VI as applicable), every exhibit listed on the exhibit index, and the Inline XBRL tagged facts within those schedules

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any schedule line not agreeing to the locked consolidation pack or its named sub-ledger source is a fail; any applicable schedule omitted, any exhibit listed but not attached, or any exhibit attached in a superseded version is a fail; zero tolerance on a missing Exhibit 97 clawback policy

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with the 10-K; test runs once per year in the pre-filing window with a light interim tie-out on the Q3 investment and reinsurance data so schedule sources are proven before year end

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared or reviewed any schedule or maintained the exhibit index

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual schedules-and-exhibits test workpaper in AuditBoard holding the schedule tie-outs, the exhibit index reconciliation, the XBRL element comparison and the exception schedule

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Tie-out binder per schedule with source extracts, the exhibit index build sheet and the auditor consent, producible for an SEC comment letter or a PCAOB inspection within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Controller drafts responses on schedule content; Investor Relations Director and General Counsel clear any SEC comment-letter reply, and the Audit Committee is informed before any 10-K/A is filed

checklist.step: Confirm which Reg S-X schedules apply this year
actions: Work through Reg S-X Article 7 and confirm applicability of Schedule I (summary of investments other than investments in related parties), Schedule II (condensed financial information of the registrant, required where restricted net assets of subsidiaries exceed 25% of consolidated net assets), Schedule III (supplementary insurance information), Schedule IV (reinsurance), Schedule V (valuation and qualifying accounts) and Schedule VI (supplemental information for property-casualty underwriters).
Compute the Schedule II restricted-net-assets test and record the numerator, denominator and result — do not carry forward last year's conclusion.
Compare the applicability conclusion to the prior-year 10-K and explain every schedule added or dropped in writing.
Circulate the applicability memo to the external audit engagement team and record their agreement.
checklist.done: a dated applicability memo shows the computed Schedule II test and a written reason for every schedule added or dropped versus prior year.

checklist.step: Map each schedule line to a named data source
actions: Build the source map: Schedule I from the investment sub-ledger and custodian valuation file, Schedule III from the reserve and DAC roll-forwards by segment, Schedule IV from the ceded reinsurance ledger, Schedule V from the allowance and valuation-allowance roll-forwards, Schedule VI from the P&C loss development data.
Name the system, report and extraction parameters for each source so the extract is reproducible.
Assign a preparer and a separate reviewer to each schedule and record the assignment in the source map.
Confirm each source system has closed for the period before extraction so the schedule is built on locked data.
checklist.done: every schedule line has a named source system, report and extraction parameter set, with a preparer and a separate reviewer assigned.

checklist.step: Build Schedule I summary of investments
actions: Extract the investment portfolio by Reg S-X category — fixed maturities by issuer type, equity securities, mortgage loans, real estate, policy loans, short-term and other long-term investments.
Populate the three required columns for each category: cost or amortised cost, fair value, and the amount at which shown in the balance sheet.
Agree the total 'amount at which shown' column to the investments line on the consolidated balance sheet to the dollar.
Explain any category where balance-sheet carrying value differs from fair value and record the accounting basis (ASC 320 classification, ASC 326 allowance).
Have the Controller review and sign the schedule tie-out sheet.
checklist.done: Schedule I totals agree to the balance-sheet investments line to the dollar and every carrying-versus-fair-value difference has a stated accounting basis.

checklist.step: Build Schedule III supplementary insurance information by segment
actions: Populate by segment: deferred acquisition costs, future policy benefits/losses and loss expenses, unearned premiums, other policy claims and benefits payable, premium revenue, net investment income, benefits and losses incurred, amortisation of DAC, other operating expenses and premiums written.
Agree each segment column to the segment footnote and each row total to the consolidated income statement or balance sheet line.
Confirm the segments used match the ASC 280 reportable segments disclosed in the footnotes — a different cut is a disclosure inconsistency.
Route the segment allocations to the FP&A Manager for confirmation that they match the internal management reporting.
checklist.done: Schedule III segment columns agree to the segment footnote and every row total agrees to the primary statements, using the ASC 280 segments.

checklist.step: Build Schedule IV reinsurance
actions: Extract gross amount, ceded to other companies, assumed from other companies, net amount and percentage of amount assumed to net, for life insurance in force and for premiums by major line.
Agree ceded premium to the ceded reinsurance ledger and to the reinsurance footnote, and agree net premium to the income statement.
Recompute the percentage-assumed-to-net column rather than carrying the spreadsheet formula forward unchecked.
Reconcile the reinsurance recoverable balance referenced in the schedule to the balance-sheet recoverable and to the NAIC Schedule F ceded reinsurance detail.
checklist.done: Schedule IV agrees gross, ceded, assumed and net to the ledger, the footnote and the income statement, with the percentage column recomputed.

checklist.step: Build Schedule V valuation and qualifying accounts
actions: Populate the roll-forward for each allowance account — premium receivable allowance, reinsurance recoverable allowance, deferred tax valuation allowance — with beginning balance, charges to expense, charges to other accounts, deductions and ending balance.
Agree the beginning balance to last year's filed Schedule V ending balance, not to a working file.
Agree the ending balance to the current balance sheet or footnote and agree charges to expense to the income statement line.
Describe the nature of deductions (write-offs, recoveries) in the footnote to the schedule rather than leaving an unexplained movement.
checklist.done: each allowance roll-forward opens on last year's filed ending balance, closes on the current balance sheet, and every deduction is described.

checklist.step: Build Schedule VI supplemental property-casualty information
actions: Populate deferred acquisition costs, reserves for unpaid claims and claim adjustment expenses, discount deducted, unearned premiums, earned premiums, claims incurred split between current year and prior years, amortisation of DAC, paid claims and premiums written.
Agree the prior-year incurred column to the reserve development disclosed in the loss reserve footnote — a difference here contradicts the footnote.
State the discount rate and the basis if any reserve discount is deducted.
Reconcile the reserve roll-forward in the schedule to the GL reserve accounts and to the NAIC Schedule P loss development triangles.
checklist.done: Schedule VI prior-year incurred agrees to the reserve footnote development and the roll-forward reconciles to the GL and to Schedule P.

checklist.step: Build Schedule II condensed parent-only financial information where required
actions: Extract the parent-only trial balance from the consolidation tool with investments in subsidiaries carried on the equity method.
Build the condensed parent-only balance sheet, statement of operations and statement of cash flows in the Reg S-X condensed format.
Agree parent-only net income and equity to consolidated net income and equity, since the equity method should produce the same result.
Disclose the restricted net assets computation and the dividend restrictions imposed on insurance subsidiaries by their domiciliary states.
checklist.done: parent-only net income and equity agree to the consolidated amounts and the restricted net assets and dividend restrictions are disclosed.

checklist.step: Build the exhibit index and confirm every exhibit exists
actions: Build the Item 601 exhibit index listing at minimum Exhibit 14 (code of ethics), Exhibit 21 (subsidiaries), Exhibit 23 (auditor consent), Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 (§302 certifications), Exhibits 32.1 and 32.2 (§906 certifications), Exhibit 97 (clawback policy) and Exhibit 101/104 (Inline XBRL).
For each index line record whether the exhibit is filed, furnished or incorporated by reference, and give the accession number and exhibit number of the prior filing where incorporated.
Open every attached exhibit file and confirm it is the current approved version, not a prior year's document.
Verify every hyperlink in the index resolves, since Item 601(a)(2) requires active hyperlinks to incorporated exhibits.
checklist.done: every index line is classified filed/furnished/incorporated with a resolving hyperlink, and every attached exhibit has been opened and version-confirmed.

checklist.step: Refresh Exhibit 97 for the Rule 10D-1 clawback policy
actions: Confirm the recovery policy still meets Exchange Act §10D and Rule 10D-1 and the listing standard: mandatory recovery of erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation received by current and former executive officers in the three completed fiscal years preceding an accounting restatement, including a Little r restatement.
Where the policy was amended, get Compensation Committee approval and record the resolution date before filing.
Confirm the two 10-K cover-page check boxes on restatement and recovery analysis are answered correctly for the year.
Attach the current policy as Exhibit 97 and hand the Compensation Committee minute reference to the Legal Counsel building the index.
checklist.done: the current board-approved clawback policy is attached as Exhibit 97 and the cover-page restatement and recovery check boxes are answered consistently with it.

checklist.step: Assemble the certifications and the auditor consent
actions: Prepare Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 in the exact Item 601(b)(31) wording — the certification text may not be edited, including the internal control paragraphs.
Prepare Exhibits 32.1 and 32.2 under 18 U.S.C. §1350 and mark them furnished rather than filed.
Circulate for CEO and CFO signature through DocuSign only after the financial statements, schedules and exhibits are final, and capture the signature timestamps.
Request the auditor's Exhibit 23 consent letter naming the correct registration statement file numbers and confirm the letter is signed and dated on or before the filing date.
checklist.done: certifications carry the unmodified statutory wording with dated CEO and CFO signatures, and a signed auditor consent naming the correct file numbers is on file.

checklist.step: Tag the schedules in Inline XBRL and review the tagging
actions: Tag each schedule fact in the filing tool against the current US-GAAP and insurance taxonomy elements, using standard elements before creating any extension.
Run the filing agent's validation and clear every EDGAR and DERA quality error, including negated-label and calculation-relationship errors.
Justify each extension element in writing — an extension used where a standard element exists is a review failure.
Compare rendered XBRL output values to the human-readable schedule page value by value before submission.
checklist.done: all schedule facts are tagged, validation errors are cleared, every extension is justified, and rendered values match the printed schedules.

checklist.step: Run the independent schedule review and sign the tie-out binder
actions: Review each schedule against its tie-out sheet, checking that each agreement is to the locked consolidation pack or the named sub-ledger, not to another schedule.
Re-foot and cross-cast each schedule and confirm prior-year comparatives agree to the prior filed 10-K.
Challenge any line with a movement over the review threshold and record the question and the answer on the tie-out sheet.
Sign each schedule tie-out sheet as reviewer and release the schedules to the audit team.
checklist.done: every schedule is re-footed, agreed to source and prior-year filings, and its tie-out sheet carries a reviewer signature with recorded challenges.

checklist.step: Clear the schedules through the external auditor
actions: Deliver the schedules and tie-out binders to the audit team by the T-15 business-day gate.
Confirm the auditor's opinion covering the schedules — the report on supplemental schedules must be consistent with the schedules as filed.
Track and close every auditor comment on the schedules with the change made or the position defended in writing.
Re-issue any schedule changed after auditor review and re-obtain the tie-out and consent alignment before filing.
checklist.done: the auditor has reviewed the final schedules, all comments are closed in writing, and any post-review change was re-cleared before filing.

checklist.step: File and retain the schedule and exhibit evidence
actions: After EDGAR acceptance, open the as-filed 10-K and confirm every schedule and exhibit on the index is present in the filed document set.
File the tie-out binders, source extracts, exhibit index build sheet, signed certifications and auditor consent into the repository under the filing year and accession number.
Apply the 7-year retention label and honour any legal hold on the period.
Confirm the index makes the records searchable by schedule number, exhibit number and accession number.
checklist.done: the as-filed document has been opened and every indexed schedule and exhibit confirmed present, with the full evidence set filed under the accession number and labelled for 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of schedules, exhibits and tagged facts
actions: Download the as-filed 10-K from EDGAR and list every Reg S-X schedule present and every exhibit on the index with its filed/furnished/incorporated status.
Export the Inline XBRL fact set for the schedule sections including element names, values, contexts and any extension elements.
Obtain the applicability memo and list the schedules management concluded were required.
Reconcile the schedules present in the filing to the applicability memo and log any required schedule not filed as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population lists every filed schedule, exhibit and tagged fact and reconciles to the applicability memo, with omissions logged.

testing.step: Reconcile schedule totals to the audited financial statements
actions: Agree the Schedule I 'amount at which shown' total to the investments line on the audited balance sheet.
Agree Schedule III row totals to the income statement and balance sheet, and its segment columns to the ASC 280 segment footnote.
Agree Schedule IV net premium to the income statement and ceded premium to the reinsurance footnote.
Agree Schedule V opening balances to the prior year's filed 10-K schedule and closing balances to the current balance sheet, and list every difference in dollars.
testing.done: each schedule total is agreed to the audited statements and prior filed schedules, with every difference quantified in dollars.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of schedule lines and exhibits
actions: Take 100% of schedule column and row totals and 100% of exhibit index lines — these are small, high-consequence populations.
Take 30 individual schedule detail lines selected at random with a recorded seed, stratified across Schedules I, III, IV, V and VI.
Take 100% of extension XBRL elements plus 25 standard-element tags selected at random.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and draw date so the selection is reproducible.
testing.done: all totals, exhibits and extension elements are covered in full plus a seeded, reproducible detail sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the schedule build from the source sub-ledgers
actions: For each sampled detail line, extract the source data yourself using the parameters in the source map rather than accepting the preparer's extract.
Rebuild the line — investment category totals, segment DAC and reserve balances, ceded premium by treaty, allowance movements — and compare to the filed value.
Reach your own conclusion on categorisation before reading the preparer's classification, particularly Reg S-X investment categories and reportable segments.
Log any difference over one dollar on a total line and any categorisation difference regardless of amount.
testing.done: each sampled line is independently rebuilt from source with an own-conclusion categorisation note and any difference logged.

testing.step: Recompute the applicability and threshold arithmetic
actions: Recompute the Schedule II restricted-net-assets test — restricted net assets of consolidated subsidiaries over consolidated net assets — and compare the result to the 25% trigger and to management's conclusion.
Recompute the Schedule IV percentage of amount assumed to net for each line.
Recompute the Schedule VI current-year versus prior-year incurred split and compare it to the reserve development table in the footnote.
Treat any arithmetic that only reconciles after an unexplained plug as a fail, not a rounding note.
testing.done: every applicability threshold and computed percentage is recomputed independently and agrees to the filed value without a plug.

testing.step: Verify the exhibit index line by line against the filed documents
actions: For each index line, open the attached exhibit or follow the incorporation hyperlink and confirm the document loads and is the version described.
Confirm Exhibit 14 matches the board-approved code version and Exhibit 97 matches the Compensation Committee-approved clawback policy version.
Confirm Exhibits 31.1 and 31.2 carry the unmodified Item 601(b)(31) wording — any edited paragraph is a fail — and Exhibits 32.1 and 32.2 are marked furnished.
Confirm the Exhibit 23 auditor consent is signed, dated on or before the filing date and names the correct registration statement file numbers.
testing.done: every exhibit index line resolves to the correct version, certification wording is unmodified, and the consent is dated on or before the filing date.

testing.step: Test the Inline XBRL tagging of the schedules
actions: Compare each sampled tagged fact's value, sign, period context and unit to the rendered schedule page.
Confirm every extension element has a written justification and that no standard taxonomy element existed for it.
Re-run the DERA and filing-agent quality checks against the as-filed instance and list any remaining error.
Log negated-label and calculation-relationship errors as exceptions rather than presentation notes, since they change the reported value.
testing.done: every sampled tag matches the rendered schedule in value, sign, context and unit, extensions are justified, and quality-check errors are listed.

testing.step: Test the deadline gates and the review sequence
actions: Recompute the 10-K due date as 60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer and compare to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp.
Compare each internal gate — schedule drafts T-25, auditor review T-15, exhibit index and consent T-7, XBRL review T-5 business days — to the actual completion timestamps.
Confirm every schedule tie-out signature and the auditor consent pre-date the filing timestamp, since evidence dated after filing cannot support it.
Flag any schedule changed after auditor review with no evidence of re-clearance.
testing.done: the filing deadline and every internal gate are recomputed against actual timestamps and all sign-offs are proven to pre-date the filing.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the schedule or exhibit, the failed attribute and the dollar difference or the missing document.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — wrong source extract, stale exhibit version, applicability not recomputed, segment mismatch, XBRL extension misuse, gate missed — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date before the next 10-K drafting kick-off, and route any post-filing schedule error to the CFO for the 10-K/A decision.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date before the next kick-off, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate by schedule and by exhibit against the zero-tolerance thresholds for omitted schedules and missing or stale exhibits.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and reviewed no schedule and maintained no exhibit index line, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any post-filing correction risk to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the evidence repository under the filing year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with per-schedule exception rates, a stated conclusion and a recorded Audit Committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Runs the audit from the company side — engagement scheduling, PBC delivery, fee tracking and the audited-financials filing; the Audit Committee holds the appointment, compensation and oversight authority and the Corporate Secretary owns the Item 407(d)(5) financial-expert disclosure

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — SOX §407 and Reg S-K Item 407(d)(5) (financial expert), SOX §301 and Exchange Act §10A(m)(3) with SEC Rule 10A-3 (audit committee independence), §10A(m)(5)-(6) (funding and advisers) and §10A(i) with Reg S-X Rule 2-01 (pre-approval and independence), re-read at each annual proxy drafting kick-off

In-scope processes.value: Annual external audit cycle: auditor appointment and independence confirmation, pre-approval of audit and permissible non-audit services, engagement planning and PBC management, audit committee communications, receipt of the audit and ICFR opinions, filing of the audited financials in the 10-K, and the Item 407(d)(5) financial-expert and Item 9(e) fee disclosures in the proxy

In-scope systems.value: Pre-approval requests, independence confirmations, AS 1301 communications and audit committee minutes held in the board portal; audited statements and the audit report filed with the 10-K in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: External Audit Coordination and Audit Committee Governance Procedure — auditor selection and rotation, service pre-approval matrix with de minimis rules, independence certification cadence, PBC and communication protocol, and the annual financial-expert determination

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Audit Committee at its first meeting of the fiscal year, with the audit committee charter re-approved annually and any change to the pre-approval matrix approved before it is applied

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Audit plan agreed by the Q3 committee meeting; audit and ICFR opinions and the AS 1301 communications delivered before the 10-K, which is due 60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer; the Item 407(d)(5) financial-expert determination and the Item 9(e) fee table are made for the proxy, filed within 120 days of year end where Part III is incorporated by reference; the auditor files Form AP within 35 days of the audit report date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal reminders 10 business days before each Audit Committee meeting for the pre-approval agenda and the independence confirmation, plus filing-tracker alerts at T-30, T-15 and T-5 business days to the 10-K for the opinion, representation letter and consent

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement letter, pre-approval resolutions, PCAOB Rule 3526 independence communications, AS 1301 required communications, management representation letter, audit and ICFR opinions, fee analysis and the financial-expert determination memo retained 7 years under Exchange Act Rule 17a-4

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Services engaged without pre-approval, prohibited-service or partner-rotation breaches, missed committee communications and any independence impairment logged with the fee amount, the affected period and the Audit Committee's disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel and the Audit Committee chair sign off on any independence impairment analysis and on any corrective or supplemental disclosure before it is filed
