Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every engagement of the principal accountant in the year (audit, audit-related, tax and all other services) with its fees, every Audit Committee meeting and minute in the year, the audit and ICFR opinions, and the filed Item 407(d)(5) and Item 9(e) disclosures

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any service performed before pre-approval, any prohibited service under Rule 2-01(c)(4), any lead or concurring partner beyond the five-year rotation, or a proxy without an Item 407(d)(5) financial-expert statement is a fail; a single fail is reported to the Audit Committee before the next filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual audit-governance test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository holding the engagement and fee population, the pre-approval reconciliation, the rotation check, the minutes review and the disclosure re-performance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Audit committee charter, independence confirmations, pre-approval resolutions with fee amounts, AS 1301 communication packs, the financial-expert determination memo and the filed disclosures, producible for an SEC comment letter or a PCAOB inspection within 5 business days

checklist.step: Confirm audit committee composition against the independence rules
actions: Test each committee member against Exchange Act §10A(m)(3) and SEC Rule 10A-3: no compensatory fee from the company other than board fees, and not an affiliated person of the company or any subsidiary.
Test each member against the listing standard's own independence definition, which is stricter, and record the conclusion per member.
Collect the annual director and officer questionnaire responses covering relationships, other directorships and family relationships, and read them before concluding.
Record the composition conclusion in the board portal with the questionnaire references, and re-test any member whose circumstances change mid-year.
checklist.done: each committee member has a documented Rule 10A-3 and listing-standard independence conclusion supported by their current questionnaire.

checklist.step: Make and document the audit committee financial expert determination
actions: Assess each member against the Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attributes: understanding of GAAP and financial statements, ability to assess the application of GAAP to estimates, accruals and reserves, experience preparing/auditing/analysing statements of comparable breadth, understanding of internal control over financial reporting, and understanding of audit committee functions.

Record how each attribute was acquired under Item 407(d)(5)(iii) — principal financial officer or auditor experience, supervision of such a person, oversight of financial statement preparation, or other relevant experience.
Where no member qualifies, draft the required explanation of why not — the disclosure cannot simply be omitted.
Confirm separately whether the named expert is independent under the listing standard and state that conclusion in the disclosure.
Get the Board to designate the named expert and record the resolution and date.
checklist.done: a determination memo maps each Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attribute to named experience for the designated expert, with an independence conclusion and a board resolution date.

checklist.step: Re-approve the audit committee charter and its authorities
actions: Check the charter grants the committee direct responsibility for appointment, compensation, retention and oversight of the auditor, and that the auditor reports directly to the committee, per §10A(m)(2).
Check it carries the §10A(m)(4) complaint procedures for accounting, internal control and auditing matters, including confidential anonymous employee submission.

Check it carries the §10A(m)(5) authority to engage independent counsel and advisers and the §10A(m)(6) company funding obligation for auditor and adviser compensation and ordinary administrative expenses.
Table the charter for annual re-approval, record the resolution, and publish the approved charter to the investor relations site.
checklist.done: the charter carries the appointment, complaint, adviser and funding authorities, is re-approved by resolution, and is published.

checklist.step: Appoint the auditor and obtain the independence communication
actions: Table the auditor appointment or reappointment for Audit Committee approval and record the resolution and the ratification item for the proxy.
Obtain the PCAOB Rule 3526 written communication describing all relationships between the firm and the company that may bear on independence, and the firm's affirmation of independence.
Discuss the communication with the auditor at the committee and record the discussion in the minutes rather than filing the letter unread.
Confirm the engagement letter names the Audit Committee as the engaging party and file the signed letter.
checklist.done: the appointment resolution, the Rule 3526 independence communication, a minuted discussion of it, and a signed engagement letter naming the committee all exist.

checklist.step: Operate the pre-approval process for every service
actions: Require every proposed engagement of the principal accountant to be entered in the pre-approval register with scope, fee estimate, service category (audit, audit-related, tax, all other) and requester before any work starts.

Screen each request against the Rule 2-01(c)(4) prohibited services list — bookkeeping, financial information systems design and implementation, appraisal or valuation, actuarial services, internal audit outsourcing, management or human resources functions, broker-dealer or investment advisory services, legal services and expert services unrelated to the audit.
Route requests to the Audit Committee for specific pre-approval, or apply pre-approval policies where the committee has adopted them with a fee cap and a reporting-back requirement.
Record the approval resolution reference and date on each register row, and block purchase-order issue until it is populated.
Report actual fees against approved caps to the committee at each meeting and seek incremental approval before a cap is breached.
checklist.done: no engagement of the principal accountant starts without a register row carrying a screening result and a dated approval reference, and fees are reported against caps each meeting.

checklist.step: Verify partner rotation and cooling-off requirements
actions: Request from the audit firm the names and consecutive years of service of the lead engagement partner and the concurring/engagement quality review partner.
Confirm neither has served more than five consecutive years and that a rotated partner observes the five-year time-out (two years for other audit partners with a seven-year limit).

Check the employment cooling-off rule: no member of the audit engagement team may have taken a financial reporting oversight role at the company within the one-year period preceding the start of the audit.
Record the confirmation with the firm's written response attached and raise the successor-partner introduction with the committee a year ahead of a required rotation.
checklist.done: written firm confirmation of partner tenure and cooling-off compliance is on file, with successor planning raised ahead of any required rotation.

checklist.step: Agree the audit plan, scope and timetable
actions: Receive the auditor's planned scope: materiality, significant risks including the presumed fraud risk in revenue and management override, scoped locations and components, and reliance on internal audit and on ICFR testing.
Compare the auditor's scoped entities and accounts to the company's ICFR scoping memo and resolve every difference before fieldwork starts.
Agree the timetable including interim fieldwork, roll-forward, PBC due dates and the opinion date, and load it onto the close calendar.
Table the plan at the Audit Committee for discussion and record the committee's input and any scope change it requested.
checklist.done: the audit plan is agreed and minuted, and the auditor's scoped entities and accounts reconcile to the ICFR scoping memo.

checklist.step: Run the PBC process and control the evidence flow
actions: Load the PBC list into the shared audit workspace with owner, due date and status on every line, and lock the folder structure so evidence lands in one place.
Deliver each item as final, reviewed support — not a working draft — and record the delivery date against the line.
Run a weekly PBC status call with the audit senior and escalate any line at risk of slipping past its due date to the Controller the same week.
Track auditor questions and management responses on a single log so the answers given are consistent across the team.
checklist.done: every PBC line is delivered by its due date with a recorded delivery date, and all auditor questions and responses sit on one log.

checklist.step: Handle audit differences and the management representation letter
actions: Maintain the summary of uncorrected misstatements with each item's amount, the affected line, and the effect on income and equity for the current and prior period.
Assess the uncorrected items individually and in aggregate against materiality under both the rollover and iron-curtain methods and document the conclusion.
Present the summary to the Audit Committee — the committee, not management, sees the full list of uncorrected differences.

Prepare the management representation letter covering the uncorrected misstatements, fraud, related parties, litigation and subsequent events, and have the CEO and CFO sign it dated the same date as the audit report.
checklist.done: uncorrected misstatements are quantified, assessed under both methods, shown to the committee, and covered in a signed representation letter dated with the audit report.

checklist.step: Take the auditor's required communications at the committee
actions: Schedule the AS 1301 communications: significant accounting policies and practices, critical accounting estimates and the auditor's evaluation of them, significant unusual transactions, difficulties encountered, disagreements with management, and uncorrected and corrected misstatements.
Take the critical audit matters the auditor intends to report in the opinion and discuss the wording before the opinion is issued.
Hold an executive session with the auditor without management present at each meeting and minute that it occurred.
Record the communications in the minutes by topic so the record shows what was discussed, not merely that a report was received.
checklist.done: the minutes evidence each AS 1301 topic by name, the critical audit matters discussion, and an executive session held without management present.

checklist.step: Receive the audit and ICFR opinions and confirm consistency
actions: Obtain the draft audit opinion on the financial statements and the opinion on internal control over financial reporting under PCAOB AS 2201.
Confirm the ICFR opinion is consistent with management's Item 9A assessment — a disagreement must be resolved before filing, not disclosed as a difference of view.
Confirm the opinion names the critical audit matters discussed with the committee and that the tenure statement showing the year the firm began serving as auditor is present.
Obtain the signed opinion and the Exhibit 23 consent dated on or before the filing date.
checklist.done: signed audit and ICFR opinions are on file, consistent with the management assessment, carrying the CAMs and tenure statement and a dated consent.

checklist.step: File the audited financial statements
actions: Assemble the 10-K with the audited statements, the audit and ICFR opinions, Item 9A and the schedules, and run the filing-agent validation.
Submit through EDGAR by the due date — 60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer — and capture the accession number and acceptance timestamp.
Open the as-filed document and confirm the signed opinions are present and legible in the filed version.
Confirm the auditor files Form AP with the PCAOB within 35 days of the audit report date and record the Form AP reference.
checklist.done: the 10-K is accepted by the deadline with the opinions confirmed present in the as-filed document and the Form AP reference recorded.

checklist.step: Draft the Item 407(d) and Item 9(e) proxy disclosures
actions: Draft the Item 407(d)(5) disclosure naming the audit committee financial expert, stating that the expert is independent, or explaining why the committee has no such expert.

Draft the Item 407(d)(3) audit committee report covering the review of the audited statements with management, the AS 1301 discussions with the auditor, receipt of the Rule 3526 independence letter, and the recommendation to include the statements in the 10-K.
Build the Item 9(e) fee table for both years split into audit fees, audit-related fees, tax fees and all other fees, reconciled to the pre-approval register and the accounts payable ledger.
State the pre-approval policies and procedures and the percentage of services approved under the de minimis exception, if any.
Route to the General Counsel and the Audit Committee chair for clearance before the proxy is filed within 120 days of fiscal year end.
checklist.done: the financial-expert statement, the committee report and a fee table reconciled to the register and the ledger are drafted and cleared by counsel and the committee chair.

checklist.step: Assess the auditor's performance and decide on reappointment
actions: Run the annual auditor evaluation survey with the Controller, entity finance leads and the committee, covering quality, industry expertise, communication, timeliness and fee reasonableness.
Read the firm's most recent PCAOB inspection report and its internal quality control findings and bring the relevant points to the committee.
Compare fees paid by category to the prior two years and explain any category with a step change.
Present the evaluation to the Audit Committee with a reappointment or tender recommendation and record the decision.
checklist.done: a documented evaluation covering survey results, the PCAOB inspection report and fee trends supports a minuted reappointment or tender decision.

checklist.step: Retain the audit governance evidence
actions: File the engagement letter, pre-approval register and resolutions, independence and rotation confirmations, AS 1301 communication packs, minutes, representation letter, opinions, consent and the financial-expert determination memo under the audit year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and honour any legal hold covering the period.
Confirm the index makes the records searchable by audit year, committee meeting date, service category and fee amount.
Run a completeness check against the committee meeting calendar and chase any meeting with no minute filed.
checklist.done: the full audit-year governance evidence set is filed under the audit year, labelled for 7-year retention, and every committee meeting has a filed minute.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements, fees and committee meetings
actions: Extract from accounts payable every invoice and accrual for the principal accountant and its network firms in the fiscal year, with vendor, entity, amount, invoice date and description.
Extract the pre-approval register for the same period with request date, category, cap and approval reference.
Extract the Audit Committee meeting calendar and minute list for the year from the board portal.
Reconcile the AP total by category to the pre-approval register total and to the Item 9(e) fee table, and explain every difference in dollars.
testing.done: the AP extract, pre-approval register and filed fee table reconcile by category with every difference explained in dollars.

testing.step: Reconcile every payment to a pre-approval that pre-dates the service
actions: Match each AP row to a pre-approval register row on scope and entity.
Compare the approval date to the earliest service date evidenced on the invoice or the engagement letter, not to the invoice date.
List every payment with no register match and every service started before its approval date as an automatic exception with the dollar amount.
Check any service claimed under the de minimis exception meets all of its conditions, including approval before completion of the audit and the 5% of total fees limit.
testing.done: every payment is matched to a pre-approval dated before the service started, or listed as an exception with its dollar amount.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of non-audit engagements — tax and all other services — since these carry the independence risk.
Take 100% of Audit Committee meetings held in the year and the full minute set.
Take 20 audit and audit-related invoices selected at random with a recorded seed.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and draw date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: all non-audit engagements and all committee meetings are covered in full plus a seeded, reproducible invoice sample.

testing.step: Re-perform the prohibited-service screening on every non-audit engagement
actions: Read each sampled engagement's statement of work and reach your own conclusion on whether it falls in a Rule 2-01(c)(4) prohibited category before reading the screening result.
Pay specific attention to actuarial services, internal audit outsourcing, valuation and appraisal, and financial information systems design and implementation, since insurance groups buy all four.
Test the management-responsibility conditions on permitted tax services — the firm must not act as management or advocate in a tax controversy before a tribunal.
Log a right-answer/wrong-basis screening as an exception, not a documentation note.
testing.done: each non-audit engagement has an independent prohibited-service conclusion with the specific Rule 2-01(c)(4) category considered and recorded.

testing.step: Re-perform the financial-expert determination against the filed disclosure
actions: Open the as-filed proxy on EDGAR and read the Item 407(d)(5) disclosure without first reading the determination memo.
Test the designated expert's biography against each Item 407(d)(5)(ii) attribute and confirm the memo maps each attribute to named experience rather than to a job title.
Confirm the disclosure states whether the expert is independent, and that the independence conclusion agrees to the Rule 10A-3 and listing-standard assessment on file.
Where no expert is designated, confirm the filing explains why not — a silent omission is a fail.
testing.done: the filed Item 407(d)(5) disclosure is independently mapped attribute by attribute to the designated expert's experience, with the independence statement verified.

testing.step: Test audit committee composition, charter and meeting evidence
actions: For each member, read the director questionnaire and confirm no compensatory fee other than board fees and no affiliate relationship, per Rule 10A-3.

Confirm the charter as published carries the §10A(m)(2) appointment authority, §10A(m)(4) complaint procedures, §10A(m)(5) adviser authority and §10A(m)(6) funding obligation, quoting the clause for each.
Read each meeting minute and confirm the AS 1301 topics were addressed by name and an executive session without management was held.
Flag any meeting where the minute records only that a report was received.
testing.done: every member's independence is verified from questionnaires, all four charter authorities are traced to clauses, and each minute evidences AS 1301 topics and an executive session.

testing.step: Trace the opinions and the consent to the as-filed documents
actions: Open the as-filed 10-K on EDGAR and confirm both the financial statement opinion and the ICFR opinion are present, signed and dated.
Confirm the ICFR opinion conclusion agrees to management's Item 9A conclusion and that any material weakness is described identically in both.
Confirm the auditor tenure statement and the critical audit matters appear and that the CAMs match those discussed at the committee.
Confirm the Exhibit 23 consent is dated on or before the filing date and check the PCAOB Form AP was filed within 35 days of the audit report date.
testing.done: both opinions are present and consistent with Item 9A in the as-filed document, CAMs match the committee record, and the consent and Form AP dates check out.

testing.step: Recompute the fee table, rotation clocks and filing deadlines
actions: Recompute each Item 9(e) fee category for both years from the AP extract and compare to the filed table line by line.
Recompute the de minimis percentage as non-pre-approved non-audit fees over total fees paid and compare to the 5% limit and to the disclosed percentage.
Recompute lead and concurring partner consecutive years from the firm's tenure confirmation against the five-year limit and the five-year time-out.
Recompute the 10-K due date at 60 days after fiscal year end and the proxy date at 120 days for Part III incorporation, and compare both to the EDGAR acceptance timestamps.
testing.done: the fee table, the de minimis percentage, partner tenure and both filing deadlines are recomputed independently and agree to the filed record.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the engagement, meeting or disclosure, the requirement missed and the fee or period affected.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — service started before approval, prohibited category not screened, rotation clock not tracked, minute not evidencing the topic, fee table misclassification, disclosure omission — and an accountable owner.

Set a remediation date before the next committee meeting that would repeat the failure, and open an independence impairment analysis with General Counsel and the firm's national office for any prohibited or unapproved service.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date before the next committee meeting, and an impairment analysis where independence is in question.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare results to the zero-tolerance thresholds on unapproved services, prohibited services, partner rotation and the missing financial-expert disclosure.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who requested no service, prepared no fee analysis and drafted no disclosure, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee in executive session at its next meeting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the audit year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with a stated conclusion against the zero-tolerance thresholds and a recorded executive-session reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the continuous SEC and state filing calendar and the timeliness evidence behind it; the Disclosure Committee chair owns the sub-certification process that supports the §302 and §906 certifications on each filing

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — SOX §302 with SEC Release 33-8124 (certification adopting release and its discussion of disclosure committees), Exchange Act Rules 13a-14 and 13a-15 (certifications and disclosure controls), 18 U.S.C. §1350 for §906, and Rule 12b-25 for late-filing notifications, re-read at each annual calendar refresh

In-scope systems.value: Filing calendar rows with owner, due date, status and confirmation attachment; sub-certification questionnaires and Disclosure Committee packs held with the filing package in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel; the Disclosure Committee charter is re-approved annually by the Audit Committee and re-approved on any change to filer status or committee membership

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: 10-K at 60 days after fiscal year end for a large accelerated filer (75 for accelerated, 90 for non-accelerated); 10-Q at 40 days (45 for non-accelerated); 8-K within four business days of the triggering event; Forms 3, 4 and 5 within 10 days of becoming an insider, two business days of a transaction and 45 days after year end; proxy within 120 days of year end where Part III is incorporated; NAIC annual statement March 1 and quarterly statements May 15, August 15, November 15

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing tracker alerts at T-30, T-15, T-5 and T-1 business days on every periodic filing row, a same-day alert to the Disclosure Committee chair on any 8-K triggering event, and a two-business-day countdown alert on every Section 16 transaction reported by the broker

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Late, amended and Rule 12b-25 filings, missed sub-certifications and unowned calendar rows logged with the form type, the days late, the cause and the disposition approved by the Disclosure Committee

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs off every late filing analysis, every Rule 12b-25 notification and the disclosure-controls conclusion that follows a missed deadline, before the next certification is executed

checklist.step: Determine filer status and the deadlines that follow from it
actions: Recompute public float as of the last business day of the most recently completed second fiscal quarter and compare it to the accelerated ($75m) and large accelerated ($700m) thresholds.
Apply the exit thresholds too, since falling below $60m or $560m changes status only under the specified conditions.
Set the periodic deadlines that follow: 10-K at 60, 75 or 90 days and 10-Q at 40 or 45 days after period end, and record the computation behind the choice.
Confirm the cover-page filer status check boxes on the next filing match the computed status.
Notify the Disclosure Committee and the Controller in writing where the status changes, because it moves every deadline for the year.
checklist.done: filer status is recomputed from public float with the calculation retained, the deadline set is updated, and the cover-page check boxes match.

checklist.step: Build the annual filing calendar row by row
actions: Create a row per expected filing for the year: 10-K, three 10-Qs, the proxy, the NAIC annual and three quarterly statements, state supplements, and standing rows for 8-K and Section 16 events.
Compute each due date from the period end using the filer-status rules and note the roll-forward convention where a due date falls on a weekend or federal holiday.
Assign a named owner and a named backup to every row and record the preparer, reviewer and signer.
Reconcile the calendar to the prior year's filing list plus any new obligation from a new state licence, a new registration statement or a new subsidiary, and record the reconciliation.
Set T-30, T-15, T-5 and T-1 business-day reminders on every periodic row.
checklist.done: every expected filing has a row with a computed due date, a named owner and backup, armed reminders, and the calendar reconciles to the prior-year filing list.

checklist.step: Charter the Disclosure Committee and fix its membership
actions: Confirm the charter, contemplated by SEC Release 33-8124, gives the committee responsibility for reviewing periodic reports and material disclosures and supporting the certifying officers.

Fix membership across the functions that hold disclosure-relevant information: Controller, Regulatory Reporting Manager, General Counsel, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Actuary, Investor Relations Director, Head of IT and Head of Compliance.
Set the meeting cadence to at least once per reporting cycle plus on demand for any material event, and name the chair and the secretary.
Table the charter for Audit Committee re-approval annually and record the resolution.
checklist.done: a re-approved charter names the committee's review responsibility, its cross-functional membership, its per-cycle cadence, chair and secretary.

checklist.step: Run the sub-certification cycle before each periodic filing
actions: Issue the sub-certification questionnaire to entity controllers, functional heads and the actuarial, claims, underwriting, investment, legal and IT leads at least 15 business days before the filing date.

Ask for positive confirmations on completeness and accuracy of reported data, known errors or misstatements, control deficiencies identified, fraud or suspected fraud regardless of materiality, litigation and regulatory matters, related-party transactions and subsequent events.
Chase every non-return through the function head and escalate any outstanding certification to the Disclosure Committee chair five business days before the filing date.
Route every exception answer to the Controller and the General Counsel for disposition before the committee meets, and record the disposition on the questionnaire.
File the completed set with the filing package.
checklist.done: a complete sub-certification set with every exception answer dispositioned is on file before the Disclosure Committee meets.

checklist.step: Hold the Disclosure Committee review of the draft report
actions: Circulate the draft report, the changes-from-prior-period redline, the sub-certification exception summary, the open litigation and regulatory matters list and the risk factor redline at least three business days before the meeting.

Work the agenda item by item: MD&A consistency with the financial statements, risk factor currency, legal proceedings, subsequent events, non-GAAP measure reconciliation and Item 9A disclosure-controls conclusion.
Record each member's confirmation that their function's disclosures are complete and accurate, and record every disclosure the committee added, changed or removed.
Reach and minute the committee's recommendation that the report is fit to file and that disclosure controls were effective, or state the deficiency found.
checklist.done: the minute records item-by-item review, per-function confirmations, disclosure changes made, and an explicit recommendation on filing and disclosure-controls effectiveness.

checklist.step: Evaluate disclosure controls and procedures for the period
actions: Assemble the inputs to the Rule 13a-15(b) evaluation as of the end of the period: sub-certification exceptions, ICFR deficiencies rated in the quarter, late or amended filings, and any restatement analysis.

Assess whether information required to be disclosed was recorded, processed, summarised and reported within the SEC's time periods, and whether it was accumulated and communicated to the certifying officers.
Assess separately under Rule 13a-15(d) whether any change in ICFR during the quarter materially affected or is reasonably likely to materially affect ICFR, and draft the Item 9A(b) disclosure.
Write the effectiveness conclusion with reasons and give it to the CEO and CFO with the supporting deficiency schedule.
checklist.done: a written disclosure-controls evaluation as of period end exists with an effectiveness conclusion, a supporting deficiency schedule and a drafted ICFR-change disclosure.

checklist.step: Execute the Section 302 and Section 906 certifications
actions: Read the final report as filed, not a draft, together with the sub-certification set, the Disclosure Committee minute and the disclosure-controls evaluation.

Sign the Rule 13a-14(a) certification in unmodified Item 601(b)(31) wording, covering the fair presentation, disclosure controls design and evaluation, ICFR paragraphs and the disclosures to the auditor and Audit Committee of significant deficiencies and fraud.
Sign the 18 U.S.C. §1350 certification alongside the CEO and confirm it is furnished as Exhibit 32.
Capture the DocuSign timestamps and confirm they pre-date the EDGAR submission — a certification signed after filing cannot support it.
File the signed certifications with the filing package.
checklist.done: both certifications are signed in unmodified statutory wording with timestamps proven to pre-date the EDGAR submission.

checklist.step: Submit and capture the acceptance evidence for each filing
actions: Run the filing-agent validation, clear every EDGAR and Inline XBRL error, and submit through EDGAR before the 5:30pm Eastern cut-off — a submission after cut-off carries the next business day's date.
Capture the accession number, the acceptance message and the timestamp and attach them to the calendar row.
Open the as-filed document and confirm the certifications, exhibits and Item 9A text are present in the filed version.
Mark the calendar row complete only once the confirmation is attached, and leave it open otherwise.
checklist.done: each filing has an attached accession number and acceptance timestamp, the as-filed document has been opened and checked, and the calendar row is closed on evidence.

checklist.step: Run the four-business-day 8-K trigger watch
actions: Maintain the trigger inventory by Item number — 1.01 material agreements, 2.02 results of operations, 4.01 auditor change, 4.02 non-reliance, 5.02 officer and director changes, 5.05 code of ethics amendments and waivers, 7.01 and 8.01 disclosures.
Instruct deal, HR, legal, treasury and finance leads to notify the Corporate Secretary the same day an event occurs, and log the event date as reported.
Compute the due date as event date plus four business days, excluding weekends and federal holidays, and open a calendar row immediately.
Convene the Disclosure Committee on demand for material events and record the materiality determination even where the conclusion is not to file.
checklist.done: every reported trigger event has a logged event date, a computed four-business-day due date and a recorded materiality determination.

checklist.step: Operate the Section 16 reporting watch for insiders
actions: Maintain the Section 16 insider list — directors, officers and 10% beneficial owners — and reconcile it to the officer roster after every appointment or departure.
Take broker transaction reports and equity-plan vesting and exercise files daily and open a Form 4 row on the trade date.
Compute the Form 4 due date as trade date plus two business days, file through EDGAR using the insider's CIK and EDGAR codes, and capture the accession number.
File Form 3 within 10 days of a person becoming an insider and Form 5 within 45 days of fiscal year end for any deferred reportable transaction.
Report any late filing to the General Counsel immediately, since it must be disclosed in the proxy under Item 405.
checklist.done: every insider transaction has a Form 4 filed within two business days with a captured accession number, and any lateness is escalated for Item 405 disclosure.

checklist.step: Escalate slippage before it becomes a late filing
actions: Review the tracker weekly for rows in amber or red against their T-15 and T-5 gates and identify the specific blocking item and owner.
Escalate any row still red at T-5 business days to the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel the same day, in writing, with the options set out.

Where the report genuinely cannot be filed on time, prepare a Rule 12b-25 notification stating the reason without unreasonable effort or expense, and file it no later than one business day after the due date.
Track the extended date — 15 calendar days for an annual report and 5 calendar days for a quarterly report — and treat it as a hard deadline.
Record the root cause of the slippage on the calendar row for the disclosure-controls evaluation.
checklist.done: every red row is escalated at T-5 in writing, any 12b-25 is filed within one business day of the due date, and the root cause is recorded for the controls evaluation.

checklist.step: Track the statutory and state filings on the same calendar
actions: Enter the NAIC annual statement (March 1), the quarterly statements (May 15, August 15, November 15), the audited statutory financial report and the actuarial opinion on the same calendar as the SEC rows.
Add the state-specific supplements and management discussion and analysis filings the domiciliary state requires, with their own dates.
Attach the NAIC submission confirmation and the state acknowledgement to each row on filing.
Reconcile the state list against the current licence register each quarter so a newly licensed state cannot go unfiled.
checklist.done: every statutory and state filing sits on the shared calendar with an attached confirmation, and the state list reconciles to the licence register each quarter.

checklist.step: Report timeliness performance to the Disclosure and Audit Committees
actions: Build the quarterly timeliness pack: filings due versus filed on time, days late by form, amendments filed, 12b-25 notifications, Section 16 late filings and open calendar rows past due.
Show the root cause distribution and the remediation status of prior-period exceptions rather than a single on-time percentage.
Present to the Disclosure Committee each cycle and to the Audit Committee quarterly, and record directed actions with owners and dates.
Feed any pattern of lateness into the next disclosure-controls effectiveness conclusion.
checklist.done: each cycle has a timeliness pack presented with root causes and remediation status, and directed actions are recorded with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Refresh the calendar and the procedure annually
actions: At fiscal year end rebuild the calendar for the new year from the recomputed filer status and the current licence and registration inventory.
Retire rows for filings no longer required and record why, and add rows for new obligations with their first due date.
Re-read Rules 13a-14, 13a-15 and 12b-25 and the current Form 8-K item list for changes and update the procedure where the rules moved.
Have the Chief Financial Officer and the General Counsel re-approve the procedure and the calendar before the first filing of the new year.
checklist.done: the new-year calendar is rebuilt from current filer status and licences, retired and added rows are explained, and the procedure is re-approved before the first filing.

checklist.step: Retain the timeliness and certification evidence
actions: File per filing: the calendar row export, the EDGAR accession number and acceptance timestamp or the NAIC confirmation, the sub-certification set, the Disclosure Committee minute and the signed certifications.
Apply the 7-year retention label under Exchange Act Rule 17a-4 and honour any legal hold on the period.
Confirm the index makes records searchable by form type, period, accession number and due date.
Run the completeness check against the calendar and chase any row marked filed with no confirmation attached.
checklist.done: every calendar row has its confirmation, sub-certification set, minute and certifications filed under a 7-year retention label and retrievable by form type and period.

testing.step: Build the population of expected and actual filings for the period
actions: Export every calendar row with a due date in the period, including owner, due date, status and attached confirmation reference.
Independently list actual filings from EDGAR full-text search for the registrant and from the insiders' filing history, covering 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A and Forms 3, 4 and 5.
Export the NAIC and state submission log for the same period.
Reconcile expected to actual and list every calendar row with no matching filing and every filing with no calendar row — the second direction catches obligations the calendar never knew about.
testing.done: expected and actual filing lists are reconciled in both directions with unmatched items on each side listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the calendar to the source of record for obligations
actions: Compare the calendar's statutory rows to the state licence register and the domiciliary state's filing requirement list and identify any licensed state with no filing row.
Compare the Section 16 insider rows to the current officer and director roster and the 10% holder list from the transfer agent.
Compare the 8-K trigger inventory to the current Form 8-K item list to confirm no reportable item type is unmonitored.
Treat any obligation present in a source of record but absent from the calendar as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the calendar is proven complete against the licence register, the insider roster and the current Form 8-K item list, with gaps logged.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of periodic reports, the proxy and all 12b-25 notifications in the period.
Take 100% of 8-K filings and 100% of Section 16 forms, since both carry short fixed clocks.
Take 15 statutory and state filings selected at random with a recorded seed, weighted to the domiciliary state.
Record population sizes, strata, seed and draw date so the selection is reproducible.
testing.done: all periodic, current and Section 16 filings are covered in full plus a seeded, reproducible statutory sample.

testing.step: Recompute every due date and compare to the acceptance timestamp
actions: Recompute each periodic due date from the period end using the filer status you independently verified from public float, not the status recorded on the row.

Recompute each 8-K due date as the triggering event date plus four business days, taking the event date from the underlying document — the contract, the board minute, the termination letter — rather than the tracker field.
Recompute each Form 4 due date as trade date plus two business days from the broker confirmation.
Compare each recomputed due date to the EDGAR acceptance timestamp and note that submissions after 5:30pm Eastern carry the next business day, then quantify days late where applicable.
testing.done: every sampled filing's due date is recomputed from primary evidence and compared to the acceptance timestamp with lateness quantified in days.

testing.step: Re-perform the filer status and 12b-25 judgements
actions: Recompute public float as of the last business day of the second fiscal quarter from the share count and the closing price and compare to the accelerated and large accelerated thresholds.
Confirm the cover-page filer status check boxes on the filed reports agree to your computation.

For each 12b-25, confirm it was filed no later than one business day after the due date, states a reason the report could not be filed without unreasonable effort or expense, and that the report followed within 15 calendar days for an annual report or 5 for a quarterly report.
Treat a 12b-25 used to buy routine time with no genuine cause as an exception, not a mitigating factor.
testing.done: filer status is independently recomputed and agrees to the cover pages, and every 12b-25 is tested for timing, stated cause and the extended-date follow-through.

testing.step: Test the sub-certification set behind each certification
actions: For each sampled periodic filing, match the sub-certification returns to the required respondent list and identify every missing return.
Confirm each return is dated before the Disclosure Committee meeting and before the certification signature.
Read every exception answer and trace it to a documented disposition by the Controller or General Counsel before the filing.
Log a certification supported by an incomplete sub-certification set as a fail against the stated threshold.
testing.done: each certification is traced to a complete, correctly sequenced sub-certification set with every exception answer dispositioned before filing.

testing.step: Test the Disclosure Committee record and the controls evaluation
actions: Read each cycle's minute and confirm it evidences item-by-item review, per-function confirmations, disclosure changes made and an explicit recommendation, not a bare attendance record.
Confirm committee membership present at each meeting matches the charter's required functions and note any cycle where a required function was absent.
Read the Rule 13a-15(b) evaluation and confirm it is as of period end, references the quarter's deficiencies and late filings, and reaches a stated conclusion.
Confirm the Item 9A(b) ICFR-change disclosure agrees to the changes actually made in the quarter per the change log.
testing.done: every cycle's minute evidences substantive review with the required functions present, and the controls evaluation is period-end dated with a stated conclusion consistent with Item 9A(b).

testing.step: Trace filings to confirmations and verify certification sequencing
actions: For each sampled filing, open the EDGAR acceptance message or the NAIC confirmation and read the timestamp rather than the tracker status field.
Open the as-filed document and confirm Exhibits 31 and 32 are present, in unmodified statutory wording, and signed.
Compare the DocuSign certification timestamps to the EDGAR submission timestamp and log any certification signed after submission as a fail.
Confirm any calendar row marked complete actually has a confirmation attached — a status field alone is not evidence.
testing.done: every sampled filing traces to a timestamped confirmation, carries unmodified signed certifications, and the signature timestamps precede submission.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the form type, the period, the days late or the missing evidence.

Assign a root cause from a fixed list — obligation not on the calendar, row unowned, event date not reported same day, sub-certification not returned, submission after the 5:30pm cut-off, statutory state not reconciled to licences — and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date before the next filing of that form type, and route any late periodic report to the CFO for the disclosure-controls effectiveness reassessment.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date before the next filing of that form, and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time rates by form type and compare to the zero-tolerance thresholds for late periodic reports without a valid 12b-25 and for late 8-Ks.

Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it and state whether the results support the disclosure-controls conclusion management reached.
Have the independent reviewer, who owned no calendar row, prepared no filing and sat on no Disclosure Committee in the period, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next meeting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the period.
testing.done: a signed workpaper exists with on-time rates by form type, a stated conclusion tied to the disclosure-controls conclusion, and a recorded Audit Committee reporting date.
